card: This pull request adds the setprunelock and listprunelocks RPCs, as well as a -prunelockheight startup argument, allowing manual management of block pruning limits. It resolves the problem on pruned nodes where unloading a wallet or taking an external indexer offline allows historical blocks needed for future rescans to be pruned away. The change exposes the existing internal BlockManager prune lock system with a user prefix, holding locks in memory across the node's runtime without persistence across restarts.
changed_since_previous: Added functional test coverage verifying that an unloaded wallet remains loadable on a pruned node when protected by a manual prune lock.
evidence: PR description: 'On pruned nodes, if a wallet is not loaded while the node is running, blocks necessary for rescanning when the wallet is loaded may be pruned. This PR allows users and external wallet software to manually manage prune locks via RPC, so they can protect blocks needed for future rescans and also clean up locks that are no longer relevant.'
Revives closed PR #19463 with updated UX patterns matching `setban`/`listbanned`.
problem: On pruned nodes, blocks needed for rescanning can be pruned if a wallet is unloaded while the node continues syncing or processing blocks. Furthermore, external wallet software using Bitcoin Core has had no mechanism to hold blocks on disk during offline periods or temporary maintenance without disabling pruning entirely.

risk.why: A flaw in prune lock logic could either prune block files required by wallets or indexes, causing rescan failures, or prevent block pruning indefinitely and exhaust disk space.

summary: Adds `setprunelock` and `listprunelocks` RPCs alongside a `-prunelockheight` startup option to allow users and external applications to manually manage block prune locks. These in-memory locks prevent the block storage manager from pruning block files at or above a specified height, using a `user:` prefix to isolate them from internal subsystem locks.
